items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Pops Foster with Darnell Howard, April 21st, 1957, reel four.

ctx.x: Yeah, take it away. Uh, all right. We want some more things, shall we tell you or shall we call down, please? Call down.

Pops Foster with Darnell Howard, April 21st, 1957, reel four. So we're going to go in the room, we're going to talk to some Spurridge. He's supposed to have a chicken come off this room, so we wouldn't have had this chicken. So put all the lights on, put the table in the middle of the floor, they'd sit over there, and I'm sitting over there on the corner. We're supposed to call him Spurridge, you know. Spurridge was supposed to come, Paul in bed. He's in bed half asleep, all the juice, and we're going to call it…
You don't have to rush time. You have to wait for this one, don't you?

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: I think they had Donnell Howell in the band too with him.

ctx.x: I'll find different spokes when I was writing. I'll find the snare drums sound more like Kittle drums. Long time ago they used to sound like a bunch of shots. Yeah. A kid.

That's what Dixon was on. Yeah, that's a short sound job. And I'll tell you, I'm going to tell you the reason that, Manuel, and you know it. Our drummers would play it in our jazz band, in our rag-tonged band those days. They tuned, they know how to tune those snares. See, you got to tune those snares. The snares got to be gauged, just like the strings on a violin, on a bass violin. They got to be tuned, and you got a row of snares on them things, and the snares all got to be correct, not too loose, they all got…

items.title: Darnell Howard Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: while I'm talking to Pop Foster here

ctx.x: Yeah, man. All the time. I should never give him-
He goes in the other room and starts yelling his head off while I'm talking to Pop Foster here. I'm getting some vital information. Did you break the show in Chicago, you mean?
